h.strategy: Borrow interaction patterns from other empirical sciences: epistasis in genetics (the effect of one mutation depends on genetic background, and beneficial mutations help fitter backgrounds less), diminishing returns in economics, and redundancy in engineered systems. Translate each pattern into a concrete conditional hypothesis about how an edit's effect varies with the parent configuration. Favor predictions that a practitioner thinking only mechanistically would get wrong, especially background-dependent sign changes and weaker gains in already-strong parents. Use conditions that many parents satisfy. In the flaw step, discard analogies that do not transfer and keep only those with a plausible general reason to hold.

hyps.why: A direct 3x3 conv path into the output already supplies conv features, so adding a second conv into node 3 yields diminishing returns.
An identity shortcut to the output eases optimization of the lengthened 0->1->2->3 conv chain, ResNet-style.
Spatial context already injected at node 2 by a 3x3 conv makes losing the 3x3 receptive field on edge 5 less costly.
With edge 0 removed node 1 is a zero tensor, so a conv on edge 4 has no signal to process.
A shallow conv into node 3 partially duplicates the existing direct 3x3 path, reducing its marginal value.
A parallel 3x3 conv into node 2 keeps its features rich, so the pooling branch acts as harmless smoothing rather than a bottleneck.
Removing the deep path when the node-1 path to the output is also absent leaves only the shallow edge-3 route, collapsing effective depth.
Without edge 4, node 1 reaches the output only via the edge 2 -> edge 5 route, so improving its features has less downstream influence.
A residual shortcut complements a strong deep conv path into the output but costs capacity when that deep path is weak or absent.
With edge 0 removed node 1 carries no signal, so a conv on edge 2 adds nothing to node 2.
